stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Inulin occurs naturally in onions, garlic, and bananas, but only in small amounts. Commercial inulin, a soluble fiber ______ chiefly from chicory root and valued by manufacturers for its mild sweetness, now appears in products ranging from yogurt to granola bars, where it can replace some of the sugar and fat without noticeably changing texture.
explanation: The subject of the main clause is "Commercial inulin," and its main verb, "appears," comes later in the sentence. The blank sits inside the appositive "a soluble fiber ______ chiefly from chicory root," which describes the fiber. That phrase needs a modifier, not a second tensed verb. The fiber receives the action (someone extracts it), so you need the past participle "extracted."

B.why: You saw that "is extracted" sounds complete next to "a soluble fiber." But it puts a tensed verb inside the appositive with no "that" or "which" to introduce it, so the sentence falls apart before it reaches the real main verb, "appears."

C.why: You probably picked this because you thought the sentence still needed a verb. It already has one, "appears," further on. "Has been extracted" adds a second tensed verb with no conjunction or relative pronoun to connect it.

D.why: You were right to choose a participle, but you chose the wrong one. "Extracting" makes the fiber do the extracting. The fiber is what gets extracted, so the passive "-ed" form is required.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: In 2019, planners in the river city of Carrow began replacing two traffic lanes along its main commercial street with tree-lined walkways and planted medians. Over the next three years, the new canopy shaded most of the remaining pavement, ______ midsummer surface temperatures along the corridor by an average of 2°C.
explanation: The main clause, "the new canopy shaded most of the remaining pavement," already has its subject and verb. What follows the comma describes the result of that shading, so it should be a modifier. Here the shading causes the cooling, so the "-ing" participle "lowering" correctly attaches the result to the clause.

B.why: "It lowered midsummer surface temperatures" is an independent clause. Joining it to another independent clause with only a comma creates a comma splice.

C.why: "Lowers" is a tensed verb with no conjunction to join it to "shaded." It also switches to the present tense in a passage about 2019 to 2022.

D.why: A clause that begins with "which" needs its own tensed verb, such as "which lowered." "Which lowering" leaves the relative clause without a working verb.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Mokuhanga, a Japanese woodblock technique ______ water-based pigments brushed directly onto the carved block, produces prints with a translucent, almost watercolor-like glow. Because the paper absorbs the pigment rather than holding it on the surface, printers must dampen each sheet beforehand and work quickly.
explanation: The subject is "Mokuhanga" and its main verb is "produces," which comes after the long appositive. The blank begins a description of the technique, so it has to be non-finite. The technique does the using, so the "-ing" participle "using" is correct.

B.why: You may have read "a Japanese woodblock technique uses" as a complete clause. But the sentence's main verb, "produces," comes later. Adding "uses" gives the sentence two tensed verbs with nothing joining them.

C.why: A relative clause is allowed here, but "that" refers to the singular "technique," so the verb must be "uses." "That use" is plural and does not agree.

D.why: "It uses" drops a full independent clause into the middle of the appositive, which breaks the sentence before it reaches "produces."

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Of the forty whimbrels ______ with solar-powered transmitters at a staging site on the Atlantic coast in 2023, thirty-one completed the journey to their Arctic breeding grounds. The tracking data revealed that most birds paused only once along the way, a finding that surprised researchers who had expected several refueling stops.
explanation: The main clause is "thirty-one completed the journey," and it comes after the long opening prepositional phrase. Inside that phrase, the blank describes "whimbrels," so it must be a modifier. The birds received the transmitters, so the past participle "fitted" is correct.

B.why: "Whimbrels were fitted" sounds like a sentence on its own, but it sits inside the phrase "Of the forty whimbrels..." A prepositional phrase cannot contain a tensed main verb. The real main verb is "completed."

C.why: Past perfect looks right because the tagging came before the journey. But the problem here is structure, not time. "Had been fitted" is still a tensed verb stuck inside a prepositional phrase.

D.why: "Fitting" makes the whimbrels do the fitting. The researchers fitted the birds, so the modifier has to be passive ("fitted").

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Portolan charts, navigational maps ______ by a web of compass lines radiating from points scattered across the sea, first appeared in Mediterranean ports in the late thirteenth century. Their coastlines were often remarkably accurate, yet inland regions were typically left almost blank, since sailors had little use for them.
explanation: The subject is "Portolan charts" and its main verb, "appeared," comes after the appositive. The blank describes the maps, so it has to be a modifier. The maps are crossed by the lines (note "by a web"), so the passive participle "crisscrossed" is correct.

B.why: "Maps are crisscrossed" adds a tensed verb inside the appositive with no "that" or "which." The sentence already has its main verb, "appeared."

C.why: Past tense suits a historical passage, but that is the trap. "Were crisscrossed" is still a second main verb, and it creates a run-on before "first appeared."

D.why: "Crisscrossing" is active, but the phrase "by a web of compass lines" tells you the maps receive the action. You need the "-ed" form.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Within hours of detecting a virus, an infected cell begins releasing interferons, small signaling proteins that diffuse into the surrounding tissue. These proteins bind to receptors on nearby cells, ______ them to produce enzymes that interfere with viral replication before the pathogen can spread.
explanation: In the second sentence, the subject is "These proteins" and the verb is "bind." The blank starts a phrase that describes the effect of that binding, so it cannot be another tensed verb. The binding causes the response, so the "-ing" participle "prompting" is correct.

B.why: "Prompt" agrees with "proteins," which is why it sounds right. But two verbs for the same subject need "and" between them. With only a comma, "bind..., prompt" is ungrammatical.

C.why: "They prompt them to produce enzymes" is an independent clause. Attaching it with only a comma creates a comma splice.

D.why: A "which" clause needs a tensed verb of its own, such as "which prompts." "Which prompting" leaves the clause with no working verb.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Between 1890 and 1910, schoolteachers in the region's rural districts were asked to write down the stories their pupils' grandparents told. The archive's most valuable holding, a set of 212 notebooks ______ preserves ghost stories and household charms that survive in no other source.
explanation: The subject is "The archive's most valuable holding" and its verb is "preserves." Between them is an appositive that opens with a comma after "holding." That appositive needs a participle, "compiled," because the notebooks were compiled. It also needs a closing comma before the main verb, so choice A is correct.

B.why: You chose the right participle but forgot the second comma. The appositive opens with a comma after "holding," so it must close with one before "preserves."

C.why: "Were compiled" puts a tensed verb inside the appositive. The subject then has two main verbs, "were compiled" and "preserves," with nothing joining them.

D.why: The comma after "compiled" separates the participle from its own "by" phrase, which is not a grammatical break. The comma that is actually needed, before "preserves," is missing.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Crown-of-thorns starfish can devastate coral reefs when their numbers surge. Their larvae, ______ on phytoplankton for several weeks before settling onto the reef, survive in far greater numbers when nutrient runoff from farmland fuels algal blooms, which may explain why outbreaks often follow seasons of heavy rain.
explanation: The subject is "Their larvae" and the main verb is "survive," which comes after the phrase set off by commas. That phrase describes the larvae, so it has to be non-finite. The larvae do the feeding, so the "-ing" participle "feeding" is correct.

B.why: "Their larvae feed on phytoplankton" sounds complete, so you may have stopped reading there. But "survive" is the real main verb, and adding "feed" gives one subject two unjoined verbs.

C.why: "Have fed" is a tensed verb inside a phrase set off by commas. It competes with the main verb, "survive," with no conjunction joining them.

D.why: "Are feeding" contains the right participle, but the helping verb "are" makes it a tensed verb. That creates a second main verb before "survive."
